chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the ransom of the game (if one eats its meat); he said: 'He eats from his sacrificial animal (Udhiyah) and gives the ransom in charity.'

key_terms.أُضْحِيَّتِهِ: His sacrificial animal (specifically the Udhiyah offered for Eid al-Adha or Hajj)
key_terms.فِدَاءِ: Ransom or expiation paid for hunting game during pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of hunted game and the required expiation (Fida')?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the dual nature of the *fida'* (expiation) for consuming hunted game: the pilgrim must eat from the meat of a sacrificial animal while simultaneously distributing its monetary value as charity. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the physical act of consumption and the financial compensation, ensuring both spiritual purification and social welfare are addressed. The emphasis on charity (*sadaqah*) reflects the broader Quranic principle of expiating sins through tangible acts of devotion and generosity.
